label.name: Name
label.errorOutput: Send errors to a separate output

tip.concurrency: Messages handled at the same time. With more than 1 the order of results is not guaranteed; set 1 when order matters.
tip.errorOutput: Errors leave through the last output labelled error instead of Catch. Use it for high-rate flows, where a Redis outage would otherwise flood the logs.
tip.legacyMsgFields: Also writes the fields of @yroshcha/node-red-contrib-redis-full (msg.streamId and others). Turn it on for a migrated node when the flow still reads those fields; keep it off for new nodes.
tip.env: Can be ${VAR}: the value is taken from the environment and the flow in Git shows where it comes from.

placeholder.clusterNodes: host:port, host:port (empty: host and port above)

tip.cluster: Cluster uses database 0. Streams with a DLQ need a hash tag, for example orders:{eu} and orders:{eu}:dlq.
tip.connections: Per pod: 1 shared connection, 1 subscriber with Pub/Sub nodes and 1 blocking connection per stream-in and list-in node.

status.unavailable: Live state needs adminAuth and a deployed config node.

tip.command: Arguments come from msg.args, for example ["user:1", "name"].
tip.allowMsgCommand: msg.command (string or array of tokens) replaces the configured command. The denylist still applies and scripts (EVAL, FCALL) are rejected.
tip.denylist: Without the denylist, FLUSHALL, CONFIG, SHUTDOWN and similar commands can run from this node. Blocking commands are always rejected.

tip.commands: msg.commands overrides this list. Every command passes the denylist.

tip.scan: Walks the cursor until the end, the result limit or the timeout. In cluster mode SCAN visits every master. HSCAN, SSCAN and ZSCAN take msg.key.

tip.subscribe: Pub/Sub only. Subscriptions are restored after a reconnect. For list queues use list in.

tip.listIn: Transitional node for list queues: popping removes the element. Delivery guarantees come from Redis Streams; this node will be deprecated after the move to Streams.
tip.prefetch: 1 pops the next element only after the flow completed the previous message. 0 means unlimited (legacy behaviour).

tip.ackMode: Manual keeps every entry in the PEL until stream ack; after a pod crash or slow processing an entry can arrive again, so downstream must be idempotent.
tip.reclaimIdleMs: Must be longer than the slowest processing of one message, otherwise another consumer takes the entry and it is processed twice.
tip.startPaused: For Kubernetes rollout: the group is created but no work is reserved until resume.
tip.batch: A batch window above 0 sends arrays: msg.payload and msg.redkern.redis.id become arrays of the same length.

tip.payload: msg.payload must be a flat object; nested objects and arrays are stored as JSON.
tip.trim: MAXLEN can remove entries still pending in a consumer group. Use stream gc for safe trimming.

tip.ack: Stream and group come from msg.redkern.redis; the fields here are fallbacks for messages without them.

tip.gc: Deletes consumers idle longer than the threshold whose PEL is empty; the check and the delete run in one script.

tip.metrics: Each sample also updates the palette metrics. With the prometheus palette they appear in its /metrics; without it on port 9551 when REDKERN_REDIS_METRICS_TOKEN is set.

tip.control: Acts on every stream in node of this runtime, or the ones matching stream, group or nodeId in the message.
